# requireNonSafeInteger

<link-summary>Returns the value after checking that it is not a safe integer.</link-summary>

<web-summary>requireNonSafeInteger() — Returns the value after checking that it is not a safe integer. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/number</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function requireNonSafeInteger<T>(
  value: T | number,
  message: string = "Expected a value that is not a safe integer."
): T;
```

An integer that an IEEE-754 double represents exactly. Beyond that range distinct mathematical integers collapse onto the same value and arithmetic quietly stops being exact.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter                                                                 | Type          | Description                                                   |
| :------------------------------------------------------------------------ | :------------ | :------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `value`                                                                   | `T \| number` | The value to validate.                                        |
| `message` _(optional)_ `= "Expected a value that is not a safe integer."` | `string`      | The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted. |

## Returns

`T` — the same value, with a safe integer excluded from its type.

## Throws

| Exception                  | Condition                    |
| :------------------------- | :--------------------------- |
| `IllegalArgumentException` | the value is a safe integer. |

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
requireNonSafeInteger(Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER + 2); // => Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER + 2
requireNonSafeInteger(1.5); // => 1.5
requireNonSafeInteger(42); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireNonSafeInteger(Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
